title: A busy backup can make a negative control pass
reproduction: Replay an absent post-act package sample with the idle marker replaced by an active backup; expire the sampling deadline.
expected: Treat a measurement overlapping a running backup as indeterminate; it may already have consumed the request.
observed: exercise(unchanged) returned 0, which main reports as PASS. Only the pre-act drain checks idle.
fix: Retain idle status with every post-act sample and reject an active or unknown state instead of awarding a pass. Record that absence is bounded by the observation window.
test_evidence: In-memory controller with mocked commands/time and a modified saved sample. All 36 genuine green after samples reported idle; the counterexample does not invalidate those results. Follow-up: 18 focused host cases plus real API34 create/unchanged. Unchanged absent in sampled idle snapshots, not evidence between samples.

title: The runner clears app state before confirming backup is enabled
reproduction: Trace an emulator with the allowed transport selected but backup disabled. Also trace a transport change between cases after the initial check.
expected: Fail before clearing any preferences when prerequisites are false; stop further seeds if environment checks fail.
observed: The first case command is destructive seed. There is no enabled-state check; the per-case transport check follows seed. Seed clears app and schedule preferences and cancels work. Even a transport refusal is caught and the next case seeds again. QEMU proves emulator, not disposable ownership.
fix: Check enabled and selected local transport immediately before each seed; abort the batch on unsafe environment changes. Require an explicit disposable-fixture acknowledgement or marker for this destructive path.
test_evidence: Read controller call order, ScheduleBackupNotificationInstrumentedTest.seed and InstrumentedTestState.resetForPassiveRootUi. No device used; the saved green run did use an enabled local transport. Follow-up: With Android backup disabled the real API34 batch stopped before seed. Empty or ambiguous prerequisites fail closed in host tests.

title: A success footer can override missing or contradictory method evidence
reproduction: Use the saved green create-act output; separately substitute a different reported method and change terminal STATUS_CODE 0 to -1, leaving the success footer.
expected: Require the selected class/method and its successful terminal record, distinct from the final runner code.
observed: Both altered outputs were accepted. The footer and blacklist do not require a per-test success or match the selector.
fix: Parse one start/terminal pair for SELECTOR with terminal status 0 and a successful final runner result; reject missing, extra or contradictory records.
test_evidence: Both in-memory parser probes accepted; unmodified green seed/act logs each contain the expected method and status pair 1,0. No fabricated result is presented as device evidence. Follow-up: Controller requires the exact scheduled method start/success; 18 focused host cases and create/unchanged on real API34 passed.

title: The held rebuild checks row count but not which row remains
reproduction: During the hold consider a one-row adapter showing the removed first source instead of the second, with storage/cache correct after release.
expected: Before unblocking the rebuild, the unselected second subscription must be the row shown.
observed: The only UI assertion during the hold is itemCount == 1. Later assertions check DAO and VPN decisions, not the held UI identity. Optional capture adds no assertion.
fix: Assert the survivor's stable list ID or exact bound label and absence of the selected ID while sync is still held.
test_evidence: Source counterexample, not an observed product failure. The actual red was 2 vs 1; the final class had eight passes. Follow-up: 11/11 connected: under a held rebuild the sole bound row was the second removal source. See assertion-followup/ under the local audit reports.

title: An invisible or wrong-row Subscribed label can satisfy the journey
reproduction: Consider a hidden recycled status TextView retaining Subscribed, or the badge bound to the incompatible row, while the DAO and later subscribed-only filter remain correct.
expected: Require a shown Subscribed badge on Visible Bulk Safe in the mixed result.
observed: The helper scans any attached child's text without checking the row name or text visibility. The production adapter can set status GONE without clearing its text.
fix: Scope the assertion to the named row and require a shown status with the exact localized label; assert the incompatible row's separate status.
test_evidence: Compared helper to DiscoverFilterListsFragment.Adapter.onBindViewHolder. Genuine final XML case passed; no wrong badge observed on a device in this review. Follow-up: 11/11 connected: exact visible localized badge for each named supported/limited-source row. See assertion-followup/ under the local audit reports.

title: A weekly named set can use the wrong day and pass the queue probe
reproduction: Trace create, setTime or rename with the expected membership/cadence/time and a different persisted weekday; leave the pending signal unchanged.
expected: Validate the named weekly day (ISO 4 in the fixture) along with time and membership.
observed: assertSet omits getScheduleWeekdayIso. Global, URL and restored-input cases have weekday checks that do not inspect this named set.
fix: Pass the intended weekday into assertSet for weekly cases and assert it after create, edit and rename.
test_evidence: Checked seed/act values, getters and the saved create queue result. This is an assertion gap, not a demonstrated scheduling failure. Follow-up: Four opt-in platform queue cases passed (eight seed/action runs). Weekly named set day 4 was checked together with its other values. See assertion-followup/ under the local audit reports.

title: Edit accepts a second rule and a disabled original
reproduction: Use an enabled new hostname on a second ID and keep the old hostname disabled on its original ID; evaluate the two production-test count queries.
expected: An edit updates the original stored rule; the old hostname should not remain for that source.
observed: The two queried counts are 1 and 0 as expected even though the original is still stored. The stronger deletion query is only applied to the other rule.
fix: Capture the edited ID before the UI action; assert the new values at that ID and absence of the old host/source independent of type and enabled.
test_evidence: Extracted the literal predicates into in-memory SQLite. The identity predicate still found one old row. ListsViewModel.updateListItem mutates the existing ID; no app defect inferred. Follow-up: 11/11 connected: edited enabled block retained its original ID; the old hostname no longer existed as a user rule. See assertion-followup/ under the local audit reports.

title: The version-reporting route points to a missing About tab
reproduction: Follow the version lookup instructions against the current More navigation.
expected: Direct a reporter to More > About to find the generated version.
observed: The old guide sent reporters to Help. That row opens an external URL, not an in-app About tab.
fix: Changed the guide to More > About.
test_evidence: Verified the label in fragment_more.xml, moreRowAbout's AboutActivity intent in MoreFragment and BuildConfig.VERSION_NAME in AboutActivity. No device run.

title: Two hash-matched README assessments describe unrelated changes
reproduction: Compare the two historical README assessments to the stated fb1bada98..c1725d8c8 path diffs.
expected: Each assessment should explain its own file's changes at the recorded digest.
observed: Both previously repeated unrelated app-guide prose from the local delta receipt.
fix: Corrected the checked-in assessments, not the frozen local receipt or either subject digest.
test_evidence: Verified both README hashes at c1725d8c8 and cdd535a52. Counted 698 recovery methods with four initial failures vs 687 in the earlier run; compared timing, missing observations and cumulative ACK descriptions with the four archived AWK scripts. No capture or platform test.

title: One index entry is not a hash-matched detailed receipt
reproduction: Join 355 index entries to the ten detailed CSVs by full path and compare the old and corrected QA receipt in Git.
expected: Attribute the original detailed review and the later correction to their own bytes.
observed: Index row 71 lacked its locator; the summary conflated the later b5a6e8fd... subject with the original e9caff98... detailed review.
fix: Added the original archive-support.csv row 2 locator and distinct digest to the later row; corrected the handoff and follow-up summary without replacing any historical subject hash.
test_evidence: Verified all ten receipt hashes and counts, 354 exact subject matches, and all 355 paths, IDs and locators. Between fb1bada98 and cdd535a52 only row 22's assessment changed. Both final-{on,off}-sets logs list Local disk image; paired assertions passed for the two schedule states.
